Manx: SCREEUYN FOSHLIT DA’N CHESHAGHT GHAILCKAGH AS FEALLAGH ELLEY TA GRIAHAGH ER CHENGEY NY MAREY. MEE VARTT, 1941.
English: AN OPEN LETTER TO THE MANX LANGUAGE SOCIETY AND OTHERS WHO ARE INTERESTED IN THE MOTHER-TONGUE. March, 1941.

Manx: Tammylt beg er dy henney, va’n Cheshaght Ghailckagh
English: The Manx Language Society, A short time ago,

Manx: ’Syn ard-valley Doolish, ny chaglym cooidjagh.
English: Held a meeting (in Douglas), (as most of you know.)

Manx: Cha row mish ayns shen, agh lhig dou gimraa,
English: In view of my absence, permit me to mention,

Manx: Cooid veg t’er my voirey neayr’s foddey dy hraa.
English: Some thought that have filled me with much apprehension.

Manx: Shoh’n Cheshaght va jeant, myr shoh ta mee cra’al
English: This Society was formed, so I now understand,

Manx: Ry-hoi nyn shenn Ghailck trooid Yn Ellan y reayll;
English: To preserve the Manx Gaelic throughout our dear land;

Manx: Dy chummal as cooney lesh brastyl ny ghaa
English: To establish Manx classes and help them along,

Manx: As greinnaghey feallagh ta loayrt yn shenn ghlare,
English: And encourage all people who speak the old tongue,

Manx: Dy ynsagh nyn gloan, lesh tushtey as graih
English: To bing up their children to love and to speak

Manx: Gailck chadjin y loayrt ny mast’ yn lught thie;
English: The Manx as ’twas spoken in hamlet and creek;

Manx: Dyn goaill urree nearey, dyn shaghney ee choiee,
English: Never to scorn it or shame it in mirth,

Manx: Agh freayll bio nyn Gailck ayns thalloo ny bioee.
English: But keep Manx alive in the land of their birth.

Manx: Ga s’ooasle va’n chooish, as feeu nyn gooid share
English: Tho’ worthy indeed was this cause to uphold,

Manx: Cre’n Cheshaght gyn-vree ta shin nish cur my ner!
English: What a feeble Society now we behold!

Manx: Myr dooyrt fer dy row, as v’eh lunagh dy jarroo,
English: As once a young member with sarcasm said —

Manx: “Bentyn rish Gailck ta’n Cheshaght shoh marroo.”
English: “As far as Manx goes, this Society is dead.”

Manx: “S’beg ta shiu jannoo son Chengey ny Marey”
English: “Tis little you do to deserve your fine name”

Manx: “As s’mooar lhishagh ve nyn moirey as nearey.”
English: “How great ought to be your confusion and shame.”

Manx: S’feer shoh as feeu, ta’n Cheshaght Ghailckagh
English: ’Tis true the Society, (when of cash there was any)

Manx: Kuse veg dy lioaryn ayns Gailck er chur magh.
English: Has published Manx books, ’tho not very many.

Manx: Agh s’beg feer ymmyd ny lioaryn shoh mie
English: But of little use these, tho’ they be e’er so good,

Manx: Mannagh beagh fer ayn lesh keeayll ad y lhaih.
English: If their true worth and meaning be not understood.

Manx: Foddee nee paart jeu rish studeyr shirveish,
English: Maybe some student will give them a place,

Manx: As ayns y Thie-Hashtee yiow paart elley reaish.
English: Or perhaps the Museum, the bookshelves to grace.

Manx: B’ee cagh elley caillt, goll naardey ’sy joan,
English: All the rest will be lost in dust and decay,

Manx: Er son nagh vel Manninee toiggal ny goan.
English: For to Manxmen their Gaelic is foreign today.

Manx: Ny-yei, ta sleih ayn foast cur graih as foays mooar
English: Yet, there still are a few with a love of the Manx,

Manx: Er Gailck as reddyn Manninagh, as arryltagh dy-liooar
DY YNSAGH glare nyn ayraghyn,
English: Who would learn with a will, (tho’ they get little thanks

Manx: DY BEAGH FIR-YNSEE AYN.
English: If there were enough teachers to help and explain.

Manx: Quoi s’lesh yn loght as nearey vooar gyn-chione?
English: Whose is the guilt and the ne’er ending shame.

Manx: Agh shegin dou cur moylley raad s’caair j’ee ve ’choyrt,
English: But I give honour to whom honour be fit,

Manx: Ga s’feer voal my Ghailck jeh’n chooish shoh dy loayrt.
English: Tho’ to do so in Gaelic, I scarcley have wit.

Manx: Va’n Ard-Ghooinney nurree ny Vanninagh dooie,
English: A Gaelic-born Manxman was President  last year,

Manx: Da’n ard-churrym shoh s’tiark fer ny s’cooie.
English: For such a high position few are worthier I fear,

Manx: She dasyn ’skyn ooilley shegin dooinyn cur booise
English: For to him above all, can we give humble thanks

Manx: Nagh vel y vooir-hraie dy-slane er ’gholl sheese.
English: That there still are a few who can speak in the Manx.

Manx: Trooid ooilley e laghyn ta’n shenn Ghooinney veen
English: Thro’ all his long lifetime, this Manxman so kind

Manx: Er graih e ghlare ghooie, er n’obbragh dy jeean,
English: And many a student, thanks God from his heart,

Manx: As shimmey fer-ynseydagh cur booise da Jee
English: Twas’ Caesar[1] himself who gave him the start.

Manx: Dy re Caesar eh-hene hoie Gailck ayns e chree.
O, dy beagh fir-elley er ve gollrish hene
English: O, if only others, like he, had done right

Manx: Cha beagh y vlaa ayns y foaynoo shoh creen.
English: The language would never have been in such plight.

Manx: Trog erriu, Y chaarjyn, my she Manninee shiuish,
English: My friends, if you are real Manxmen, arise!

Manx: Gow greim er Gailck choud’s t’ee foast er-mayn diuish.
English: Get hold of the Manx ere the native tongue dies.

Manx: S’coan Manninee dooiey, s’feer shenn t’ad gaase
English: Manx speakers are few, and ’tis old they are growing

Manx: Goll raad ny feilley, sheese yn ughtagh gy-baase.
English: In the way of all flesh, down the hill they are going.

Manx: Shione mie dou dy jarroo yn aght ta shiu g’ennaght
English: Now I know very well what some of you say,

Manx: “S’cair da ve Gailck ayms, nee’m gynsagh laa-ennagh.”
English: “I ought to have Manx, I’ll learn some day.”

Manx: As jir feallagh elley, smoo daaney, “Cha nee,”
English: And others will shamelessly say, “What’s the use,”

Manx: “Cha vel veg ry-chosney voish Gailck aghterbee.”
English: “Twill profit me nothing.” (O futile excuse.)

Manx: Ta fys aym myrgeddin dy vel Caggey ayns nish,
English: I am quite aware, too, of the War we’re in now.that there is a War now,

Manx: Agh shoh dy ve leshtal, cha vod shiu goaill-rish.
English: Though such for excuse you can hardly allow;

Manx: Ta shiuish syn Ellan foast baghey ayns shee,
English: In the Island you live as though there were peace,

Manx: As s’beggan ta boirey nyn gadley ’syn oie.
English: And little disturbs you when day’s labour cease.

Manx: ERSOOYL TRAA DY LIOOAR AS LHIGGEY MY HRAA,
English: SO AWAY WITH EXCUSES AND PROCRASTINATION,

Manx: B’EE AD MOLLAGHT-MYNNEY NY HELLAN DY BRAA?
English: SHALL THEY BE FOR EVER THE CURSE OF OUR NATION?

Manx: Juan y Gell,
English: John Gell,

Manx: Purt Ellesmere,
English: Ellesmere Port,

Manx: Sostyn.
English: Wirral.

Manx: [1] Caesar Cashin (1856-1943)
